faq.a: Urbanisation is the growth in the share of people who live in towns and cities rather than in the countryside. Urban means to do with towns and cities; rural means countryside.

faq.q: When did more people live in cities than in the countryside?
faq.a: Around 2007, according to the United Nations. Before then, most people in human history lived in the countryside.
asks: When did the world become mostly urban?
When did more people start living in cities?

faq.q: Why do people move to cities?
faq.a: People move from the countryside to cities for jobs, higher pay, schools, hospitals and services. Low farm incomes and droughts can push them out of villages. This is called rural-urban migration.
In Africa and Asia. Cities such as Lagos, Kinshasa, Dar es Salaam, Dhaka and Delhi are growing fast, while most people in Europe and the Americas already live in cities.

faq.q: What problems can fast urbanisation cause?
faq.a: When cities grow faster than homes, roads, water and sewers can be built, people may live in crowded informal settlements, and traffic and pollution grow. But cities also bring jobs, schools and new ideas.

facts: According to the UN, in 1950 about 30% of the world's people lived in urban areas.
The UN estimated that urban dwellers passed 50% of the world population around 2007.
In 2018 the UN projected that 68% of people would live in urban areas by 2050.
